thread:
maya: Hey team - saw a weird latency bump on TP all-reduce today during the nightly perf run. Small-msgs (~256B) tail latency jumped ~3.5x after the kernel-selector rollout. Investigating.
aj: can you paste the perf run id / job link?
maya: job: https://ci.internal/reports/TP-regen/2026-03-17/42 (perf run)
maya: quick numbers from the microbench (repro on 8xA100, batch=1):\n```\n# run_allreduce_microbench --mode=tp --msgsize=256 --iters=200
avg_latency_ms: 1.2\np99_latency_ms: 9.8 (baseline ~2.6 before rollout)\n`\n
sam: who flipped the kernel-selector flag? I saw a change that prioritizes 'fastpath-pack' for kernel selection on small msgs.
toni: that was me - trying to reduce CPU scheduling overhead. I didn't expect a regression in NCCL handoff / redispatch.
aj: can we confirm redispatch frequency? If kernel choice fails at handshake it might requeue and cause extra allreduce hops.
maya: dug into traces: lots of "kern_switch -> redispatch" around the time of the spike. Also noticed KV cache eviction spikes concurrently (cache miss growth ~x4).
sam: interesting - maybe the new kernel path reduces local batching so more fragments enter the network, hitting NCCL with smaller messages -> ring inefficiency?
toni: hypothesis: fastpath-pack tries to avoid coalescing to keep latency low, but that increases RPCs between TP ranks and leads to more rendezvous and loss of comm/compute overlap.
aj: can you paste the trace snippet? maybe include the small stack/annotation.
maya: paste: \n```\n[trace] 0.0001s: prepare_fragment(size=256) -> select_kernel(fastpath-pack)\n[trace] 0.0002s: enqueue_allreduce -> handshake(start) -> nccl_send_small_chunk\n[trace] 0.0048s: kern_switch(reason=oversub) -> redispatch(kernel=ring->tree)\n[trace] 0.0095s: kvcache_evict(key=prefix123)\n```\nsam: that sequence lines up. If redispatch causes additional kernels to be scheduled later, we lose overlap and see p99 explosion.
toni: rollback flag on a canary then? I can revert the selector change for tonight's run.
aj: before rollback, can we try a controlled repro with `--no-redispatch` toggled to see if it's redispatch or kernel choice? Also measure comm/compute overlap with perf counters.
maya: repro command I used: `./tools/tp_micro --ranks=8 --msg=256 --iters=200 --profile=flame` - I'll run with `--no-redispatch` now and post numbers.
infra-bot: CI job queued: perf-repro-1769999999-no-redispatch (will run on 8xA100 pool)
maya: results: avg=1.25ms p99=2.8ms with --no-redispatch (much closer to baseline)
sam: that points at redispatch being the culprit. But still odd that KV cache evictions spike - maybe redispatch timing misaligns KV cache lifecycle and causes prefix misses.
aj: can we add an instrumentation point in KV cache to log `last_used_ts` and eviction reason for those keys during microbench? low overhead sampling.
toni: I'll add a lightweight sampling patch and run a short 60s test.
maya: sample results: 60% of evictions during spike labeled `evict_prio=redispatch_wait` and keys were small prefixes from same tensor group.
sam: so chaining: kernel-selector -> fastpath-pack -> increased fragment bursts -> redispatch -> kvcache eviction bursts -> extra network noise -> p99 spike.
aj: mitigation ideas: 1) make kernel-selector aware of KV cache pressure and avoid fastpath when prefix-hits are hot, 2) tune redispatch backoff to batch a few failed attempts before switching, 3) re-enable coalescing for small_msgs when TP mode.
toni: I'll prototype #2 (redispatch backoff) and #1 as a policy flag. Prototype should be quick.
maya: can we also add a perf test that runs with varied msgsize sweep (128B..4KB) to find cliff points and automated alert if p99 degrades >1.5x after kernel changes?
aj: yes, add to nightly perf and gate selector rollouts behind it.
toni: pushing a patch with backoff and policy flag to PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/492 (small change, unit tests included)
infra-bot: PR 492 CI: build passed, perf smoke failed (expected), but full perf queued.
maya: thanks. For triage notes: we should treat redispatch as higher-risk in TP than in DP because of handshake/rendezvous frag choreography. I'll write up a short mitigation doc and add rollback if perf regression >1.3x in canary.
aj: +1. Good catch. Nice trace work, maya. :rocket:
toni: will follow up tomorrow with numbers on canary and rollout plan.
maya: thanks all. I'll file a followup incident note with the perf graphs and a reproducible script in \nhttps://docs.internal/ops/tp-allreduce-repro.md\n
